title: Fragment provenance & sentinel reconciliation for truncated streamed JSON tool outputs
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem:
When LLM responses are streamed and intended to be strict JSON (or a function call payload), truncation or partial tokens can produce unparseable fragments. Existing resume/repair heuristics (bracket balancing, escape trimming) are brittle and diverge between SDKs. This ticket proposes a lightweight fragment provenance and sentinel reconciliation scheme that: (1) lets the model emit small, machine-recognizable fragment markers alongside payload chunks, (2) provides a client-side verification and repair strategy using checksums and soft-end markers, and (3) includes a compatibility fallback for older models that do not emit sentinels.

Goals:
- Reduce false-positive parse failures after network truncation or mid-token termination.
- Make resume semantics idempotent and verifiable across retries.
- Avoid changing existing API payload shapes for users who don't opt-in.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full protocol rewrite for streaming (we keep the same envelope).
- Not proposing mandatory wire-level changes that break older SDKs; compatibility mode required.
acceptance_criteria: Spec merged into docs repo (doc link) describing sentinel format and reconciliation steps
Runtime can emit fragment sentinels when configured; end-to-end integration test shows a truncated chunk is reparable in 95% of test cases
SDK client library implements verify/repair with deterministic heuristics and badge for 'synthetic-repaired' responses
Backward compatibility: for older models without sentinels, SDK fallback passes existing unit tests and adds two new heuristics (escape-normalization, minimal padding)
Performance: added checks add <1ms median overhead per chunk at 4k token throughput in local microbenchmarks
design_notes:
Sentinel strategy (high level):
- Each chunk MAY terminate with a tiny sentinel JSON object on its own data channel or as an adjacent envelope token: {"__rw_fragment":true, "seq": <int>, "parent": <short-id>, "crc16": <hex>, "soft_end": <true|false> }
- The sentinel is always ASCII-safe and intentionally short so it does not skew tokenization heavily.
- Clients verify crc16 over the preceding chunk payload. If mismatch or the tracer indicates mid-token truncation, client will: 1) attempt incremental escape normalization, 2) if parse still fails and soft_end==true, append minimal closing tokens (]}") or inject "partial":true marker into the last object, 3) mark payload as 'synthetic-repaired' and emit telemetry.
- For tool/function calls, we treat the fragment sentinel as part of the envelope not the function args. If sentinel indicates seq gap, client will request resume with 'resume_after_seq' and server will replay from last confirmed seq.

Compatibility fallback (no sentinel):
- Heuristic order: 1) bracket/brace balancing with escape-aware scanning; 2) attempt to unescape a trailing partial escape sequence and reparse; 3) attempt minimal padding of common closers ("}","]") and reparse for up to 3 variants; 4) if still failing, attempt to wrap payload in a container {"__partial_repaired":true, "content":<raw string>} and surface to caller for best-effort downstream handling.

Telemetry & safety: Whenever synthetic repair happens, emit a structured event with fields: parent, seq, repair_strategy, crc_ok (true|false), repaired (true|false). Mark customer_impact low unless repair rate > 0.5% per hour.

Open trade-offs considered:
- CRC length vs tokenization cost: chose crc16 over crc32 to keep sentinel short while still catching most corruption.
- Whether to make sentinel mandatory: decided opt-in to avoid breaking incrementally deployed models/clients.
- Whether to inject repair markers into user-visible payload: prefer a wrapper/meta field so downstream callers can opt-in to strict-mode parsing.
implementation_plan: runtime: add optional fragment sentinel emission flag (config: "emit_fragment_sentinals") and minimal crc16 computation (ENG/runtime changes)
sdk: implement verify_and_repair(chunk, sentinel_opt) routine with deterministic heuristics and public API flag (allow_synthetic_repair)
tests: fuzz harness covering token-level truncation across languages and encodings; assert parseability after repair in sentinel and fallback modes
docs: publish design doc + migration guide for partners (include example best-practices for function-calling flows)
rollout: feature flag to enable on host for a small % of traffic, monitor repair telemetry, increase incrementally
comments:
2025-06-13 | Aisha Kapoor: Spiked a quick PoC: runtime emits sentinel as "
{...}
" on a separate side-channel and SDK can consume. CRC16 computation on GPU path adds ~0.4ms per chunk. Results in PR #7890.

2025-06-14 | Priya Deshmukh (review): Concerned about using control chars as separators in some client environments (mobile JS). Suggest switch to printable prefix '<<RWFRAG>>' or require side-channel over SSE meta events.

2025-06-15 | Marco Ruiz: Updated plan to prefer printable sentinel prefix and to support both inline-sentinel and SSE-meta modes. Added fallback heuristics for environments where side-channel is unavailable.
2025-06-16 | Security (Danielle Yu): Quick review - no secrets in sentinel, CRC only. Approve for opt-in use. Flag: ensure telemetry is scrubbed for PII if payloads are included.

2025-06-18 | Engineering (Ben Carter): Implemented SDK repair routine. Found edge-case: nested string containing closing bracket sequence causes false-repair. Added escape-aware scanner to reduce false positives. Draft PR linked.

2025-06-20 | Product (Leah Kim): Prioritizing for the next runtime release because enterprise customers reported parsing failures after network reconnection. Please add migration note for Dedicated customers about feature flag toggles.
